freshness_policy.rule: A programme may be labelled live only when an official primary source currently exposes an application, registration or active product surface. Live records require verified_at and next_review_at. Amounts, fees, rates and deadlines are displayed only when a cited primary source supports the claim.
freshness_policy.stale_rule: If next_review_at is in the past, the public UI must downgrade the record to review_due and must not present it as currently live until re-verified.

programmes.name: Uwezo Fund — Wezesha Loan
programmes.window_note: Uwezo Fund states that there is no application deadline because it is a revolving fund.
programmes.eligibility_summary: Registered eligible groups applying through their constituency, with a group bank account and the required youth/women/PWD membership and leadership composition.
programmes.application_method: Complete the Uwezo Fund loan application and submit it to the relevant constituency office; the online Uwezo loan portal also exposes a Start Applying path.

programmes.name: Uwezo Fund — Endeleza Loan
programmes.window_note: Uwezo Fund states that there is no application deadline because it is a revolving fund.
programmes.eligibility_summary: Repeat borrowers that completed and properly used the Wezesha loan and meet the published group requirements.
programmes.application_method: Complete the Uwezo Fund application and submit it through the constituency process with evidence of completion of the initial loan.

amount.label: Graduated repeat financing up to KES 500,000

programmes.name: Women Enterprise Fund — Tuinuke Chama Loan
programmes.window_note: The official product page currently invites eligible groups to apply through WEF constituency offices; no fixed closing date is stated on that page.

geography.coverage_note: WEF states that services are available in all 290 constituencies.

programmes.eligibility_summary: Registered self-help groups of 10–30 women aged 18+, registered for at least three months, with an active commercial bank account and WEF financial-literacy training.
programmes.application_method: Visit the nearest Women Enterprise Fund constituency office, complete the loan form and submit the required group and bank documents.

programmes.name: Youth Enterprise Development Fund — Group Loans
programmes.window_note: The official YEDF product and application-form pages currently expose group loans and application forms; no fixed closing date is stated.
programmes.eligibility_summary: Registered groups with at least five members, at least 70% youth aged 18–34 and 100% youth leadership, plus a group bank account and required application documents.
programmes.application_method: Use YEDF loan application forms and submit through Youth Fund county offices; YEDF states that county offices guide vetting, training and repayment steps.

amount.label: Group financing graduates from KES 100,000 up to KES 1,000,000

programmes.name: Youth Enterprise Development Fund — Asset Finance Loan
programmes.window_note: The official product page currently publishes the asset-finance facility; no fixed closing date is stated.
programmes.eligibility_summary: Youth entrepreneurs seeking business assets; financed assets serve as primary security and additional security may apply for some asset classes.
programmes.application_method: Access Youth Fund services through county offices and the published loan application process.

amount.label: Up to KES 5,000,000; YEDF finances up to 75% of eligible asset value

programmes.name: Youth Enterprise Development Fund — VIBE Blue Economy Loan
programmes.window_note: The official YEDF VIBE product page is currently published; no fixed closing date is stated.
programmes.eligibility_summary: Youth seeking to start or grow qualifying blue-economy ventures, including fisheries, aquaculture, marine tourism, maritime transport and related activities.
programmes.application_method: Use the Youth Fund loan application process and county offices for assessment and submission.

programmes.name: Kenya Industrial Estates — Industrial Credit
programmes.window_note: KIE currently exposes an online funding form and industrial-credit service; no fixed closing date is stated.
programmes.eligibility_summary: Businesses in manufacturing/value addition and qualifying services; working-capital applicants generally require an operating track record and appraisal under KIE rules.
programmes.application_method: Submit the official KIE online funding form or engage a KIE branch for appraisal.
programmes.terms_note: Official KIE pages currently show differing loan-range figures. The Finder therefore withholds a single headline amount and directs applicants to confirm current terms with KIE.

programmes.name: Access to Government Procurement Opportunities (AGPO)
programmes.window_note: The official AGPO portal currently exposes account registration and access to tender information.
beneficiaries: enterprises owned by persons with disabilities
programmes.eligibility_summary: Eligible Kenyan enterprises owned by youth, women or persons with disabilities and meeting the published business-registration, ownership and compliance requirements.
programmes.application_method: Register through the AGPO portal and complete business and compliance information; certification enables access to preference and reservation opportunities.

programmes.name: Hustler Fund — Group Loan
programmes.window_note: The official Hustler Fund currently exposes the Group Loan product and USSD access path.
programmes.eligibility_summary: Group members must meet the published Hustler Fund onboarding requirements; groups have at least 10 members and use the supported mobile-network/USSD process.
programmes.application_method: Create or join a group and apply digitally through USSD *254# / the supported Hustler Fund channel.

amount.label: Group limit up to KES 1,000,000, subject to scoring and product rules
